title: How I check whether an AI-assisted tower icon still reads at match size in Rampartloom
author: Uzunn
selftext:
I’m the developer of Rampartloom. One part of my workflow uses OpenAI image generation for tower and research icons. The hard part for me is deciding which detail a player actually needs: a painted mushroom cap can look great on its own, but several purple caps side by side can all read as the same button.



I’ve been comparing Spore’s models up close and from the overhead match angle, with textures on and off. For the icons the question I want to answer is whether someone can pick a tower from the build bar, place it, and recognize it on the board without reopening its tooltip. How do you test that handoff between an icon and its model in your own games?



If you want to try it, the Spore tutorial is in the free Windows demo: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5629600/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5629600/)



Some visuals, music and voiceovers were made with generative AI tools. Nothing is generated during gameplay.

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: I would show a new player the build bar for a few seconds with tooltips hidden. Then ask them to point to the matching tower on the board. If they mix two towers up, I would change the silhouette or main color before adding more detail. Have you tried it at phone size too?
